questions.q: Which is NOT a property of white noise?
options: Values depend on the previous value
why: This is a property of white noise.
This is a property of white noise.
Correct: in white noise, values do not depend on earlier values.
This is a property of white noise.

questions.q: How do you build a random walk from white noise?
why: Correct: y(t) = y(t-1) + shock is a running total of shocks.
Differencing does the opposite: it turns a walk back into noise.
A square root does not create dependence between time points.
An average of noise is still noise-like and not a walk.

questions.q: The last value of a random walk without drift is 120. What is the best forecast for 5 steps ahead?
questions.why: Future shocks have mean zero, so the best forecast at any horizon is the last value, 120.

questions.q: A random walk with drift 0.5 ends at 30. What is the forecast for h = 4?
You forecast a random walk with σ = 2. By what factor does the interval half-width grow from h = 1 to h = 25?
questions.why: Width is proportional to sqrt(h). sqrt(25) / sqrt(1) = 5.

questions.q: A colleague says: 'The price series has a clear upward trend over 200 days, so I will fit a line and extrapolate.' The price is a random walk. What is the main problem?
options: The line has too few parameters.
The trend is random and has no reason to continue.
Prices cannot be forecast with lines in Python.
why: The number of parameters is not the issue.
Correct: a random walk can drift far in one direction by chance, and the direction can change at any time.
A line can be fitted in Python. The issue is that it is a wrong model.
A random walk is not white noise. Its differences are.

questions.q: After you fit a model, the residuals pass a white noise check. What do you conclude?
options: The model left no simple autocorrelation pattern in the residuals.
You do not need a test set.
why: Correct: the residuals look random, so the model used the linear pattern in the data.
White residuals still have random errors. The error is not zero.
Residuals can be white for a model of non-stationary data too.
You always need a test set to measure future error.
